item.title: (USA-NY-Queens) Employee Relations Manager, Human Resources
item.description: Employee Relations Manager, Human Resources **POSITION DETAILS** Queensborough Community College seeks an Employee Relations Manager who is motivated to coach, guide, and support employees, supervisors, and leaders across a diverse, mission-driven campus community. The Office of Human Resources provides responsive, high-quality service in recruitment, benefits, performance management, classification, compensation, and employee relations. Our work is grounded in partnership, trust, and a Culture of Care that supports employees as they serve our students and community. The Employee Relations Manager will help strengthen workplace relationships, resolve concerns with fairness and care, and support managers in leading effectively. This role is ideal for a thoughtful, proactive HR professional who enjoys coaching others, navigating complex conversations, and developing practical solutions that foster a respectful, inclusive, and productive workplace. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted resource to employees, supervisors, and senior leaders, providing guidance with professionalism, discretion, empathy, and confidentiality. The Employee Relations Manager will support employee relations matters from intake through resolution, conduct thorough and impartial investigations, advise on HR policies and best practices, and partner with campus offices to address concerns thoughtfully and consistently. We are looking for someone who is service-oriented, skilled at building trust, and committed to helping people do their best work. The ideal candidate brings sound judgment, emotional intelligence, strong communication skills, and a coaching mindset. They will be comfortable working with employees at all levels, translating policy into clear guidance, and advancing a workplace culture rooted in accountability, respect, inclusion, and care. Key Responsibilities The Employee Relations Manager will: Serve as the primary point of contact for employee relations matters, including intake, investigation, follow-up, and resolution of workplace concerns, while maintaining confidentiality, objectivity, and compliance with applicable laws and institutional policies. Conduct impartial investigations and facilitate timely, fair resolutions using best practices, mediation, and problem-solving approaches. Advise and guide managers and supervisors in addressing employee performance, conduct, attendance, and workplace behavior concerns, including progressive discipline, corrective action, and appropriate documentation, consistent with applicable policies and collective bargaining agreements. Collaborate with College Counsel, the Office of Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging, the Office of Public Safety, and other campus partners on employee and labor relations matters. Manage the employee accommodation process in accordance with ADA requirements, including intake, facilitation of the interactive process, and employee notifications. Coach and advise employees, managers, and senior leaders on workplace concerns, team dynamics, respectful communication, conflict resolution, and performance management. Coordinate and monitor compliance training programs, including ESPARC, Workplace Violence Prevention, and Gender-Based Violence Training, ensuring accurate records and adherence to applicable requirements. Identify trends in employee relations issues and recommend proactive strategies to enhance workplace culture, engagement, and retention. Develop and maintain employee relations reports and tracking mechanisms to monitor workplace concerns, identify trends, evaluate resolution outcomes, and inform data-driven recommendations and institutional decision making. Develop, coordinate, and facilitate training and professional development programs on conflict resolution, communication, leadership, compliance, performance management, and inclusive workplace practices Promote a Culture of Care by modeling respectful dialogue, supporting employee well-being, and helping managers create environments where employees feel heard, valued, and accountable. Maintain and update the QCC Human Resources website to ensure alignment with current legislation, CUNY policies, and institutional practices. Participate in committees and special projects in support of Human Resources and broader institutional initiatives. This position follows a hybrid work schedule, requiring a minimum of 70% on-campus presence and 30% remote work over a two-week period, subject to departmental operational needs and applicable institutional policies. This position is excluded from union representation. CUNY is an equal opportunity employer committed to increasing the diversity of its workforce. We welcome applications from members of protected groups, including minorities, women, veterans, individuals with disabilities, and others who would bring valuable perspectives to the University’s mission. Candidates with a demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusion through research, teaching, service, or professional practice are encouraged to apply. One of Queensborough Community College’s greatest strengths is the diversity of our community, and we strive to attract and support talented faculty and staff who reflect the unique character of Queens, the most diverse county in the United States. **QUALIFICATIONS** Bachelor's Degree and six years' related experience required. **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** The preferred candidate will bring significant employee relations experience, strong subject matter knowledge, and the ability to communicate with clarity, confidence, and care. We are especially interested in candidates who can coach others, build trust across diverse groups, and support a workplace culture rooted in respect, accountability, inclusion, and service. The preferred candidate will have: + Relevant experience in human resources or labor relations, preferably in higher education and/or a unionized environment; + Current knowledge of local, state, and federal employment laws and labor relations practices, including Title VII of the Civil Rights Act, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), and the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA); + Demonstrated ability to prepare clear written materials, including investigation reports, employee resolution process responses, and position statements; + High emotional intelligence and the ability to manage sensitive and complex matters with diplomacy, discretion, confidentiality, and care; + Experience in assessing and resolving personnel matters, advising and coaching managers and senior leaders, prioritizing competing assignments, and making sound, timely decisions; + Experience developing or facilitating employee training, professional development, or performance management programs; + Experience evaluating employee accommodation requests in compliance with ADA requirements, including intake, the interactive process, and employee notification; + Experience working in a diverse setting; and + Proficiency in Microsoft Office and working knowledge of HRIS platforms, preferably PeopleSoft and/or Workday. **CUNY TITLE OVERVIEW** Manages a portfolio of Human Resources programs and operations at the College level. - Assumes responsibility for delivery of one or more human resources programs, which may include recruitment, performance management, labor relations, pay administration, recordkeeping, and/or human resources technology - Manages staff responsible for carrying out operations in the Human Resources office - Directly supports College department chairs and managers in staff planning, recruiting, hiring, and resolving sensitive personnel issues regarding their employees - Provides guidance on the impact of laws and regulations, CUNY policies, and collective bargaining agreements - Provides outreach to employees and provides communications such as meetings, newsletters, and web sites - Compiles accurate and well-organized reports - Assists management with developing policies, procedures, and programs to support Human Resources' objectives - Performs related duties as assigned. Job Title Name: HR Manager **CUNY TITLE** Higher Education Associate **FLSA** Exempt **COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS** The salary range is $109,898 - $129,041 commensurate with education, qualifications and experience. CUNY's benefits contribute significantly to total compensation, supporting health and wellness, financial well-being, and professional development. We offer a range of health plans, competitive retirement/pension benefits and savings plans, tuition waivers for CUNY graduate study and generous paid time off. Our staff also benefits from the extensive academic, arts, and athletic programs on our campuses and the opportunity to participate in a lively, diverse academic community in one of the greatest cities in the world. **HOW TO APPLY** Visit www.cuny.edu, access the employment page, log in or create a new user account, and search for this vacancy using the Job ID or Title. Select "Apply Now" and provide the requested information. Candidates must provide a resume andshould include a cover letter. **CLOSING DATE** December 14, 2026. Review of resumes to begin immediately. **JOB SEARCH CATEGORY** CUNY Job Posting: Managerial/Professional **EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY** CUNY encourages people with disabilities, minorities, veterans and women to apply. At CUNY, Italian Americans are also included among our protected groups. Applicants and employees will not be discriminated against on the basis of any legally protected category, including sexual orientation or gender identity. EEO/AA/Vet/Disability Employer. Job ID: 33189 Location: Queensborough CC Job Type: Full-Time

item.title: (USA-NY-Queens) Integrated Advisor, CUNY Inclusive Economy Initiative (Student Career Program Manager) - Multiple Positions
item.description: Integrated Advisor, CUNY Inclusive Economy Initiative (Student Career Program Manager) - Multiple Positions **POSITION DETAILS** The CUNY Inclusive Economy Initiative at Queensborough Community College seeks Integrated Advisors to create career pathways and expand employment opportunities for students in New York’s emerging industries. You will work with Industry Employment Specialists to support a cohort of undergraduate students, connecting them with relevant internship or full-time opportunities in a selected industry. Queensborough's focus areas are Psychology, Health Sciences, and Business Administration. **Build a Community:** + Provide both group and 1:1 activity designed to help students identify career goals, academic courses, and goal-oriented career opportunities + Develop your cohort’s identity as a peer network + Help students plan for internships and other opportunities to build their experience in and exposure to workplaces + Assess students’ professional abilities and development at several points throughout the cohort. **Establish a Peer Network:** + Participate in CUNY-wide professional development and mentoring + Collaborate between academic/career advisors and academic departments on insights from employers that might influence curricula and individual student progress. **Create Pathways:** + Identify barriers to student success within areas of study related to career goals + Share information on student needs and connect them to supportive services and campus resources + Expand student exposure to careers and the courses needed to prepare for them + Coordinate programs to enhance job-seeking skills. **Portfolio Management:** + Create plans for your cohort’s structure of programs, assessments, advising, and referral activities + Track progress, challenges and outcomes using state-of-the-art technology to measure success and make adjustments in real-time **Data Entry, Outcome Tracking, and Reporting:** + Enter data accurately and consistently into databases (i.e. Power BI, SharePoint, and Microsoft Dynamics) + Use the full Microsoft Office Suite, including Excel, to facilitate, manage, track, and report on program outcome metrics + Conduct, manage, and evaluate events via Zoom (or a similar platform), including creating registration, engaging participants during the workshop, and analyzing post-session attendance and other data This position follows a hybrid work schedule, requiring 70% on-campus presence and 30% remote work over a two-week period, subject to departmental operational needs and applicable institutional policies. CUNY is an equal opportunity employer, is committed to increasing the diversity of its workforce and is dedicated to recruiting and retaining professionals who share the College’s commitment to equity. It welcomes nominations of, and applications from members of protected groups including minorities, women, veterans and individuals with disabilities, as well as others who would bring additional perspectives to the university’s mission. Candidates with demonstrated commitment to diversity and inclusiveness through their research, teaching and/or service are also encouraged to apply. One of Queensborough Community College’s greatest strengths, and a necessary element of excellence, is the diversity of our community. We strive to attract and nurture a talented and diverse faculty and staff that proudly reflect the unique character of the local Queens community, the most diverse county in the United States. **QUALIFICATIONS** Bachelor's Degree and six years' related experience required. We seek motivated, flexible, and resourceful people who can gain the confidence of others in an advising environment and execute successful programs. Candidates will have the following preferred qualifications: • Coursework or training related to adult development, including career development • Experience in academic advisement or career coaching • Ability to facilitate job-related services, workshops, and skills trainings • Understanding of academic programs, majors, and methods to ensure students’ successful progress • Understanding the needs and practices of employers in recruitment and selection • Command of Microsoft Suite and Zoom • Comfort with technology to track programs and projects. **CUNY TITLE OVERVIEW** Develops and manages career development programs and services in a College of Unit and assumes a leadership role in the design and delivery of creative approaches to career education and planning. - Assists in unit planning, such as setting goals and objectives, and monitors status of progress toward meeting goals - Designs and produces outcomes assessment reports; reviews outcomes and feedback and recommends strategies to expand and improve services. - Directs a portfolio of targeted career programs, such as mentoring, internship, and alumni programs - Manages one or more aspects of career office operations, such as on-campus recruiting - Evaluates new technologies, assessment materials, and other career tools, makes recommendations, and acquires/implements them - May counsel a limited number of students - Performs related duties as assigned. Job Title Name: Student Career Program Manager **CUNY TITLE** Higher Education Associate **FLSA** Exempt **COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS** $94,017. Salary commensurate with education and experience. CUNY's benefits contribute significantly to total compensation, supporting health and wellness, financial well-being, and professional development. We offer a range of health plans, competitive retirement/pension benefits and savings plans, tuition waivers for CUNY graduate study and generous paid time off. Our staff also benefits from the extensive academic, arts, and athletic programs on our campuses and the opportunity to participate in a lively, diverse academic community in one of the greatest cities in the world. **HOW TO APPLY** Visit www.cuny.edu, access the employment page, log in or create a new user account, and search for this vacancy using the Job ID or Title.
